result.rationale: The migration inserts raw values from the old embeddable_hosts site setting via SQL (`INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`), which bypasses EmbeddableHost's `before_validation` normalization (`self.host.sub!(/^https?:///, '')`). Since `record_for_host` compares `lower(host) = ?` against a bare `uri.host`, migrated values with protocol prefixes or paths would never match, silently breaking embedding for pre-existing hosts. This is a real defect verifiable from the diff.

adjudication.rationale: In the migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts`, hosts are copied from the old `site_settings` value via raw SQL: `INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)` without running the `EmbeddableHost` model’s `before_validation` normalization that strips `http(s)://` and paths. Later, embed authorization uses `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)` which parses the URL and compares `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)`. If migrated rows contain values like `http://example.com` or `https://example.com/1234`, they will not equal `example.com` and will fail to match, breaking allowed-host checks after upgrade for such stored values.
